question: Can the novel images produced by convolutional diffusion models be explained and predicted from first principles as the optimal empirical score subject to locality and translation-equivariance, rather than as imperfect memorization by an opaque neural network?

key_findings.claim: An exact empirical score on a finite training set is a memorizer, so creativity must arise from a structured failure to learn that unconstrained optimum.
key_findings.evidence: The forward distribution is a Gaussian mixture centered on shrunken training images. Its exact score is a posterior-weighted force toward those images; the deterministic reverse probability flow exactly recovers the empirical distribution, and positive feedback concentrates the posterior on one training example.

anchors.section: 2 The ideal score machine only memorizes

key_findings.claim: The minimum-MSE local score (LS) replaces one global training-image posterior with an independent posterior for every pixel based only on a local patch at that same spatial location.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 7-8 condition each pixel's force on its neighborhood and sum over co-located training patches. Distant pixels with disjoint receptive fields can therefore commit to different training images, turning one global memorization decision into many coupled local decisions.

key_findings.claim: Adding translation equivariance yields a closed-form equivariant local score (ELS) in which any generated patch can select a matching patch from any image and any spatial position in the training set.
key_findings.evidence: Equations 9-10 sum over the dictionary of every patch with the prescribed shape. The appendix derives this as the functional optimum of score matching under a shared local function, and Theorem B.2 separately shows that a general equivariant optimum is the empirical score of the group-augmented dataset.

anchors.section: B.1 Optimal local translationally equivariant score matching

key_findings.claim: Zero padding partially breaks equivariance and gives boundaries a mechanistic anchoring role in generation.
key_findings.evidence: A patch containing padded zeros reveals whether it is at an interior, edge, or corner position. The boundary-broken ELS therefore restricts each pixel to a location-compatible patch dictionary; circularly padded MNIST produces more texture-like and less spatially anchored outputs in both theory and experiment.

key_findings.claim: At convergence, the local machines generate locally consistent patch mosaics rather than arbitrary images or single memorized examples.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.1/B.3 states, assuming the reverse trajectory and its derivative have limits and the nearest patch is unique, that every output pixel equals the central pixel of the closest eligible training patch to its generated neighborhood. A two-image black/white example shows exponentially many configurations satisfying the resulting majority-color constraint.

anchors.section: 4 A theory of creativity after convergence and 4.1 toy example
B.4 The sample distribution at t=0 under a local score approximation

key_findings.claim: The calibrated local-score machines predict individual samples from small convolution-only diffusion models with very high pixelwise agreement when given the same initial noise.
key_findings.evidence: With 20 theory steps and 150 neural-network steps, Table 1 reports best per-dataset median pixelwise r2 values of 0.94 for MNIST, 0.95 for CIFAR10, 0.94 for FashionMNIST, and 0.96 for CelebA over 100 matched seeds per configuration. The corresponding ideal-score memorization baselines are much lower.

key_findings.claim: The effective locality scale is coarse early in denoising and contracts toward 3x3 at late times, which the paper uses to explain fine-scale structural mistakes.
key_findings.evidence: Input-output Jacobian heatmaps and a calibration sweep show large receptive fields at high noise followed by monotonically smaller chosen patch sizes, reaching 3x3 for the last steps. FashionMNIST samples and their ELS counterparts share extra or missing limbs; the explanation is that late local decisions cannot coordinate the global limb count.

anchors.section: 5.1 Coarse-to-fine time dependent spatial locality scales and 5.3 Spatial inconsistencies

key_findings.claim: The analytic theory is not parameter-free: its time-indexed patch-size schedule is selected retrospectively from neural-network validation trajectories.
key_findings.evidence: At every reverse step, the authors compare neural-network noise predictions with ELS machines across candidate scales by cosine similarity, then choose the median optimal scale over validation samples. They explicitly state that they have no a-priori method for predicting this schedule.

anchors.section: 5.1 Coarse-to-fine time dependent spatial locality scales

key_findings.claim: Non-local self-attention weakens but does not erase the local patch-mosaic signal.
key_findings.evidence: On a public CIFAR10 UNet with self-attention, unchanged ELS predictions have median r2 about 0.77 on 100 matched seeds versus 0.48 for the ideal-score baseline. Qualitative pairs suggest attention often carves a coherent object from a less coherent local mosaic, but the paper leaves a theory of that operation open.

anchors.section: 6 The relation between theory and attention

key_findings.claim: The reported correlations establish a strong predictive surrogate for these trained models, but do not by themselves prove that the neural networks internally implement the exact Bayesian patch-posterior algorithm.
key_findings.evidence: The derivation identifies the score-matching optimum inside a constrained function class, while experiments compare outputs and receptive-field scales. There is no internal causal intervention showing that trained filters store or explicitly select the derived patch dictionary; equally predictive approximations could in principle share the same output geometry.

anchors.section: 5 Tests of the theory on trained models

method.core_idea: Begin with the closed-form score of a finite empirical image distribution, then project it onto function classes that are local, translation-equivariant, or partially boundary-conditioned; use the resulting analytic posterior-over-patches dynamics as a mechanistic surrogate for trained convolutional diffusion models.
method.mechanism: The exact empirical score is a softmax-weighted sum of forces toward all noised training images. Restricting each output pixel to a neighborhood replaces the global posterior with a pixel-specific posterior over local patches. Enforcing translation equivariance shares the local scoring function across positions and expands the eligible dictionary to translated patches; zero padding narrows that dictionary according to visible boundary context. The reverse DDIM flow then assembles a sample through interacting local patch commitments. To compare with neural networks, the authors train small zero- or circular-padded ResNets and UNets, estimate a time-varying effective receptive field, calibrate the analytic patch size at each step, and compare paired outputs from identical initial Gaussian noise using pixelwise r2.
assumptions: The relevant inductive biases of convolution-only diffusion models are adequately summarized by spatial locality and translation equivariance.
Trained models are close to the minimum-MSE empirical score within the selected constrained function class.
A square patch and a single scale at each reverse time adequately approximate a network's heterogeneous effective receptive field.
The calibrated locality schedule generalizes from validation trajectories to the 100 evaluated noise seeds.
Euclidean distance between noised patches is the relevant similarity statistic for local generative decisions.
Twenty-step deterministic reverse integration accurately represents the analytic machine; convergence claims additionally assume trajectory and derivative limits and a unique nearest patch.
Pixelwise r2 on matched-noise samples is an informative measure of mechanistic prediction even when perceptual quality or distributional fit is not evaluated.
Zero values in padded context reveal boundary position with probability one under the continuous noising model.
Small 32x32 datasets and deliberately normalization-free CNNs isolate mechanisms that transfer meaningfully to more practical diffusion systems.
The ideal empirical score is the right memorization baseline for distinguishing structured underfitting from exact finite-data fitting.

techniques.role: Expresses exact finite-dataset denoising as a posterior-weighted Gaussian-mixture score and supplies the memorization baseline.
Derives the minimum-MSE score subject to pixelwise receptive-field constraints.
Shares the local rule across positions and selects from the full translated training-patch dictionary.
Models zero-padding as partial equivariance breaking that restricts eligible patches by interior, edge, or corner context.
Characterizes limiting generated images through nearest-patch central-pixel fixed points.
Selects a patch scale at each denoising time by cosine matching analytic and neural score predictions.
Feeds identical initial noise and class labels to analytic and neural samplers, then measures pixelwise r2 per image.
Tests circular versus zero padding and a pretrained self-attention UNet to probe the limits of the locality/equivariance account.

evaluations.setting: Zero-padded, class-conditional CIFAR10 ResNet; 100 matched noise seeds; 20 analytic and 150 neural reverse steps
evaluations.metric: Median pixelwise r2 between ELS and neural samples
evaluations.result: 0.95, with ELS outperforming the ideal-score baseline on 100% of samples
evaluations.baseline: Ideal-score machine median r2 is 0.42; local-score median is 0.90

evaluations.setting: Zero-padded ResNets on MNIST, FashionMNIST, and CelebA with the same matched-seed protocol
evaluations.result: ELS reaches 0.94 on MNIST, 0.94 on FashionMNIST, and 0.96 on CelebA

evaluations.setting: Zero-padded UNets on MNIST, CIFAR10, FashionMNIST, and CelebA
evaluations.metric: Median pixelwise r2 over 100 paired samples
evaluations.result: Best local theory reaches 0.89, 0.90, 0.93, and 0.90 respectively; CelebA is the one case where fully local LS beats boundary-broken ELS

evaluations.setting: Circularly padded ResNets on MNIST and CIFAR10
evaluations.metric: Median ELS pixelwise r2 and fraction beating ideal score

evaluations.setting: Public self-attention-enabled CIFAR10 UNet, using the locality schedule calibrated on a convolutional CIFAR10 ResNet
evaluations.metric: Median pixelwise r2 over 100 matched seeds
evaluations.result: 0.77 for ELS and ELS beats ideal score on 95% of samples

evaluations.setting: All architectures with both analytic and neural samplers restricted to 20 reverse steps
evaluations.result: Correlations generally decline—for example CIFAR10 ResNet from 0.95 to 0.90 and CIFAR10 UNet from 0.90 to 0.82—while remaining above ideal-score baselines
evaluations.baseline: Table 1 uses 150 neural steps; the authors report no theory for why that mismatch improves agreement

limitations: Reviewer-identified: the locality scale is a fitted time series selected from neural validation trajectories, not predicted from architecture, dataset, or optimization a priori.

Reviewer-identified: experiments use small, normalization-free ResNets and UNets on 28x28 or 32x32 images; latent diffusion, text conditioning, large-scale data, and modern DiT backbones are outside the demonstrated regime.
Reviewer-identified: the self-attention test is only one public CIFAR10 UNet and falls to median r2 about 0.77, leaving the paper without an analytic account of non-local semantic coordination.
Reviewer-identified: pixelwise r2 on paired seeds measures samplewise imitation but not likelihood, FID, precision/recall, diversity, semantic correctness, or human-perceived creativity.

Reviewer-identified: the theory assumes the trained network reaches the constrained score optimum; output agreement does not establish that its internal computation literally enumerates Bayesian patch posteriors.
Reviewer-identified: ELS evaluation requires access to a training-patch dictionary and does not establish computational scalability to large images or datasets.

Reviewer-identified: the local-consistency theorem assumes limiting trajectories and derivatives exist and that the nearest patch is unique; finite-step integration can violate consistency, as the paper's toy example shows.
Reviewer-identified: 'exponentially many' real-image mosaics are not counted or bounded; the explicit demonstration is a highly special two-image black/white toy system.
Reviewer-identified: class conditioning, the learned time embedding, and optimization dynamics are not derived; they enter only through the trained comparison networks.
Reviewer-identified: agreement improves when the neural model uses 150 reverse steps but the analytic model uses 20, and the source explicitly says no theoretical explanation is known.

Reviewer-identified: the explanation of extra limbs from late locality is plausible and samplewise predictive, but no intervention that enlarges late receptive fields tests whether the artifacts causally disappear.
Reviewer-identified: the model treats local Euclidean patch similarity as sufficient and therefore does not model perceptual invariance, object identity, or long-range relations directly.
failure_modes: An exact ideal score collapses every trajectory to a training image and therefore cannot account for novel finite-data samples.
An overly small late-time patch size makes distant body parts commit independently, yielding extra or missing limbs and other global inconsistencies.
Circular padding removes boundary anchors and can turn localized digits into texture-like arrangements.
A ResNet whose maximum receptive field is smaller than the image cannot use distant boundary information to infer absolute position.
A UNet with global receptive field can break equivariance more completely than boundary-broken ELS predicts, as on CelebA.
Self-attention can reorganize a local patch mosaic into a semantically coherent object that the local theory cannot fully predict.
Coarse numerical integration can converge to samples that violate the theorem's local-consistency condition.
Nearest Euclidean patches may be locally plausible but compose into a globally impossible scene.
reusable_insights: Derive a memorizing empirical optimum first, then identify which architectural constraints convert its global posterior into decoupled local decisions.
Use the same random seed as a strong casewise test of a mechanistic generative theory; distribution-level similarity alone can hide wrong trajectories.
Treat padding as an information channel and an architectural prior, not a neutral implementation detail.
Measure effective receptive fields over denoising time rather than assigning one static locality scale to an architecture.
A useful creativity audit can label every generated region with its nearest eligible source patch and then measure where local consistency conflicts with global semantics.
Separate a fitted explanatory surrogate from a prospective theory: freeze its calibration on one split and test new architectures, datasets, resolutions, and seeds.
Intervene on late-time locality or add controlled global communication to test causal explanations of structural artifacts.
open_questions: Can the time-dependent locality schedule be predicted from receptive-field geometry, training-set patch statistics, model capacity, and noise level without fitting neural trajectories?
Does increasing only late-time global communication causally reduce limb-count and other compositional errors while preserving diversity?
How should the ELS posterior be generalized from Euclidean patches to learned perceptual features without forfeiting analytic tractability?
Can a comparable case-by-case theory explain attention, cross-attention conditioning, latent autoencoders, and diffusion transformers?
How many genuinely distinct mosaics are supported by a real training set after overlap constraints are enforced, and how does that count scale with patch size?
Can source-patch attribution distinguish benign recombination from privacy leakage or near-copying at different spatial scales?
Will a locality schedule calibrated at one resolution, dataset size, or training checkpoint predict another prospectively?
What internal causal evidence would discriminate explicit patch-posterior computation from another function that happens to yield similar output trajectories?
Can one jointly optimize local creativity and global coherence using a controlled mixture of ELS-like and attention-like score components?

competitive_landscape.title: Towards a Mechanistic Explanation of Diffusion Model Generalization
competitive_landscape.difference: Niedoba et al. independently infer a local denoising bias and aggregate local empirical denoisers to imitate networks across forward and reverse processes. Kamb and Ganguli additionally impose/derive equivariance, model padding-specific boundary dictionaries, prove a local-consistency result, and report stronger paired-output claims for convolution-only networks; the concurrent work is an important priority limit on locality as the core idea.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning multi-scale local conditional probability models of images
competitive_landscape.difference: Guth et al. explicitly build multiscale local Markov score models over wavelet coefficients and show that small conditional neighborhoods can capture faces. The target paper instead derives local/equivariant optima in pixel space and uses them to predict independently trained CNN outputs seed by seed.

competitive_landscape.title: Closed-Form Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Scarvelis et al. deliberately smooth the exact empirical score and use a nearest-neighbor estimator to produce novel samples without training. The target paper obtains novelty by locality/equivariance constraints and seeks to explain trained convolutional networks rather than propose a practical smoothed sampler.

competitive_landscape.title: How Compositional Generalization and Creativity Improve as Diffusion Models are Trained
competitive_landscape.difference: Favero et al. model hierarchical composition rules and derive polynomial sample complexity for progressively longer coherence scales in text and images. The target paper explains creativity through spatial patch recombination and architectural locality at a fixed trained model, but does not derive how data size determines learned global coherence.

competitive_landscape.title: Breaking the Curse of Dimensionality: Diffusion Models Efficiently Learn Low-Dimensional Distributions
competitive_landscape.difference: Zhang et al. equate diffusion training on low-rank Gaussian mixtures with subspace clustering and obtain sample complexity linear in intrinsic dimension plus semantic directions. Kamb and Ganguli instead analyze finite receptive fields and translated image patches, producing a casewise predictor but no finite-sample learning theorem.

competitive_landscape.title: Diffusion Models Generate Images Like Painters: an Analytical Theory of Outline First, Details Later
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang and Vastola solve a Gaussian probability-flow approximation and explain high-variance outlines appearing before low-variance details, including pretrained latent models. The target paper's coarse-to-fine variable is spatial receptive-field size and its main contribution is exact paired prediction for small CNNs from training patches.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper provides the first analytic, mechanistically interpretable theory that predicts creative outputs of trained convolutional diffusion models case by case from locality and equivariance, and explains them as locally consistent patch mosaics.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It derives closed-form LS/ELS/boundary-broken scores, proves a convergence constraint, calibrates one time-varying locality scale, and obtains median pixelwise r2 up to 0.96 over matched-noise samples across two CNN families and four datasets.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The distinctive contribution is the combination of equivariant local-score derivation, boundary mechanics, a limiting local-consistency theorem, and unusually strong paired-seed prediction. Local empirical denoising and multiscale-local explanations were concurrent or prior, so locality alone is not novel. The fitted scale schedule and small-CNN regime also make this a high-quality mechanistic surrogate rather than a complete theory of diffusion creativity.

reviewer_notes: Complete primary full-text pass over all 37 cached pages, including the analytic derivations, theorem assumptions, model/training details, both quantitative tables, and all comparison appendices. Six adjacent or competing works were checked directly on current primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23. Author claims and reviewer inference are explicitly attributed. The source's strongest evidence is the paired-noise evaluation over 100 seeds per configuration; its central scope constraint is equally explicit: the patch-size trajectory is calibrated from the network and no a-priori scale theory exists. A secondary verifier should reproduce several r2 rows from the public code and audit validation/test separation in the locality-scale calibration before promotion to verified.
